previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and known coronary artery disease presented with recurrent chest pain that awoke him from sleep, relieved by nitroglycerin. Evaluation revealed new EKG changes and a positive pharmacologic stress test showing a reversible perfusion defect in the RCA/LCx territory. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which confirmed 90% stenoses in the right coronary artery at the edge of a prior stent and in the mid-distal segment. Rotational atherectomy was performed, followed by placement of two drug-eluting stents. The procedure was successful with no complications. He remained chest pain-free post-procedure, completed a dialysis session, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dual antiplatelet therapy and resume his regular hemodialysis schedule.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with history of presumed gout, ESRD s/p failed transplant 
___, presenting with one day of severe right knee pain whose 
exam and history is concerning for MSK injury. 

# RIGHT KNEE PAIN:  Patient reported acute onset of severe right 
knee pain when pressing on brakes of his car ___ and despite 
being worked up for infection in the ED, identified this as his 
chief complaint. He presented unable to bear weight and had 
limited active and passive ROM due to pain as well as pain on 
palpation of superior, medial, and lateral aspects of the joint. 
The patient reported a history of gout flares but medical 
records show no crystal confirmation of the diagnosis and the 
knee was not red, swollen or signs of allodynia. Allopurinol had 
been discontinued as outpatient due skepticism of history of 
gout. Given these symptoms, there was little concern for septic 
arthritis. Film study from ___ showed no change in knee from 
baseline but could be consistent with possible subchondral 
insufficiency fracture or osteonecrosis of the bone, whose 
findings are less clear on XRay than MRI. Ortho consult has seen 
patient and reviewed the film studies and recommended pain 
control for osteo arthritis with outpatient follow up with Dr. 
___.  ___ medical team spoke with Dr. ___ on the 
phone who agreed that MRI was not indicated patient was 
scheduled for outpatient follow up. While osteonecrosis of the 
knee could cause acute-onset severe monoarticular knee pain, 
ultimately felt to be unlikely. Prior to d/c, evaluated by ___, 
who recommended follow up at outpatient cardiac rehab, where his 
walking would be addressed. 

#ILD/DYSPNEA: Patient initially reported history of SOB, 
productive cough, and subjective fever in presentation to ED on 
___, concerning for viral illness. In ED he had mild fever in 
the setting of dialysis (99.4) and CBC showing leukocytosis. CBx 
were sent off and were negative to date. Flu swab was negative. 
CBC on ___ showed neutrophilic leukocytosis but WBC count 
quickly resolved.  No signs of infection on CXR noted and no abx 
were started. 

 #LEUKOCYTOSIS: Patient initially presented with neutrophilic 
leukocytosis and inconsistent initial complaints of subjective 
fever and chills, which patient denied once he arrived on floor. 
In the setting of a resolving leukocytosis, process thouht to be 
likely due to stress reaction and did not represent an acute 
infectious or inflammatory process such as gout.

#CAD: Recent admission for chest pain where patient underwent 
left heart catheterization on ___ revealing 90% stenoses of his 
RCA at the proximal edge of an existing stent and the mid-distal 
vessel.  Cardiac enzymes drawn in ED and were 0.06, which is 
likely negative in the setting of ESRD and elevated creatinine. 
EKGs showed no ischemic changes and on exam his chest pain was 
recreated with palpation, suggesting MSK in origin. He also 
shows no signs of hemodynamic instability on history or exam. He 
was continued on home medications (ASA, Plavix, and 
atorvastatin). Recommended for cardiac rehab on disposition.
